Nagpunit ng Meralco bills ang mga miyembro ng Gabriela para kundenahin ang mataas na singil sa kuryente, sa inilunsad na Black Friday Protest sa Quezon City, Pebrero 20. 

Paliwanag ng grupo, dapat ibasura ang 12% value-added tax na lalong nagpapataas ng presyo ng mga pangunahing bilihin at singil sa serbisyo gaya ng kuryente. 

"Lagi na lang ang mga konsyumer ang pumapasan ng kahit anumang galaw sa presyo ng kuryente--sa generation man, transmission, o distribution," pahayag ni Clarice Palce ng Gabriela. 

Binigyang-diin din ng Gabriela na dapat ibasura ang Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA). Paliwanag nila, inalis ng batas ang kontrol ng pamahalaan sa sektor ng kuryente at hinayaan ang mga pribadong kumpanya na magpatakbo nito. | Adrian Puse/Altermidya

data.raw_text:
Web3 gaming doesn’t have a tech problem. It has a focus problem if you ask me.

Everyone keeps shipping for the same Western PC crowd same Discord funnels, same wallet-first onboarding that scares normal players away.

Meanwhile, 3.5B mobile gamers are already out there… and most of Web3 barely sees them.

@elympics_ai did. What did they really do?
Instead of launching another token treadmill, they went after the unsexy layer: infrastructure.

• Server authority to stop client-side manipulation • AI anti-cheat analyzing behavior in real time • Proof of Game so results match actual gameplay • Public replays anyone can audit

Not just bare promises systems and they didn’t box themselves into one chain either. They integrated Top blockchains like TON, Abstract, Base multichain from day one.

For me the real shift is economic.

Play-to-Earn inflated supply until everyone raced to exit. Play-to-Win flips it: zero-sum tournaments where entry fees fund prizes. Winners earn from performance, not emissions.

That’s why the early data matters.

• @PenguClash just closed Season 27 after running four themes in four weeks plus weekend tournaments and thousands of soulbound mints for active players.

• Plooshy Pileup is quietly pulling tens of thousands of uniques with steady daily growth.

• Smash and Crash on Abstract? Pure physics skill. No RNG excuses.

All built for fast sessions, mobile play, Telegram access, web access pure cinema 

When you look into it the thesis gets even clearer:
- Mobile gaming is a $90B+ machine. - India is overwhelmingly mobile-first. - Southeast Asia lives on phones. - Latin America runs on messaging apps. - Cities like Lagos and Manila aren’t waiting to buy gaming PCs.

People open an app. They play. They compete with friends.

Elympics is building for that reality local payments, social tournaments, on-chain records without forcing users to “learn crypto” first.

Web3 gaming can keep fighting over the same small pond… or it can build for the billions already playing.
